accuracy.evidence: Checked against the PSHE Association KS1 programme of study (medicines and household products; people who help keep us safe), NHS 'Accidental poisoning' advice (keep medicines and chemicals out of reach; call 111, or 999 if drowsy, not breathing well or fitting; keep the packet) and CAPT guidance that under-5s are most at risk and liquid laundry capsules look like sweets. The red-bordered diamond is the CLP/GHS hazard pictogram used on household chemicals. The lesson never says that every unsafe product carries a sign (the shampoo card and m4 say the opposite), and calls vitamins medicine. Parameterised answers n*0 are 0 at every corner.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the beliefs named in poisoning-prevention guidance and the adult text: telling sweets from tablets by looking (look-alike predict, pairs scene, m1, challenge 'look'), friends' or siblings' medicine will help me (give predict, give feedback, rule card, m2, challenge 'share'), more medicine works better (rule card feedback, p2, m3, challenge 'more'), no warning sign means safe (red diamond predict, shampoo feedback, m4, challenge 'nosign'), and picking up a found tablet or pod to help (found scene 'Pick it up and carry it' feedback, p3, m5, challenge 'touch').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagmeds is about this topic's own decisions: identical-looking pairs that only flip to food or not food when tapped, a medicine bottle with three candidate givers in three places, bottles drawn with and without the red hazard diamond sorted into drink or not, a found tablet, bottle or pod with three actions, and medicine rule cards. It shares no mechanism with flagsafe (roads, hot things) or flagtrust (who to tell, secrets), and the lab_distinct gate keeps it under 30% against every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers the key idea by doing: the pairs only reveal what they are after a tap, and the twin message says 'Same look, not the same thing'; dropping shampoo into Drink is refused with 'No sign does not mean safe'; choosing a child or 'help yourself' as the giver gets a reason. Done messages confirm the rule only after the task.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong answers that the lab then disproves: 'Yes, I can tell' (every pair looks identical until flipped), 'Yes, it helped her' (the give scene refuses Jo, the big sister and the cousin with the reason that medicine is only from a trusted grown-up for you), and 'Yes, no sign means safe' (shampoo has no diamond and is still refused as a drink).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions, each wrong option tagged with its slip and a specific message: look, share, more, nosign, touch and who (for example 'Do not touch or taste it. Leave it and tell a grown-up.'). Lab feedback also names the slip: 'is a child, not a grown-up who looks after you', 'Big children are still children', 'Never taste something you find', 'Do not pick it up, even to help'.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs are short sentences with everyday words (poorly, tablets, juice, cleaner, red diamond) and one rule each; validate_lessons readability passes. Canvas text is two short banners per scene, e.g. 'You find: Tablets on the floor.' then 'What do you do?'.

no_filler.evidence: Every kid sentence is a rule, a reason or an example; adult paragraphs give curriculum placement and the under-5 risk, the habit to teach and storage advice, the common mistakes with what to do if a child swallows something, and the lab scenes. The content gate finds no filler phrases.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px screenshots in light and dark for every scene: look-alike cards are about 150 x 90 px, the giver cards have wrapped names, the bin titles were shortened to 'Drink' and 'Not a drink' after the first screenshot clipped them, sorted bottle names list inside each bin, and the rule cards use 2 columns at 11 px after a 3-column draft was too small.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: each look-alike, each giver ('Dad gives me the medicine'), each bottle to Drink or Not a drink, each of the three actions, and each rule card to Safe or Not safe. The canvas aria-label updates with every message, challenge feedback is a polite live region, and the walk gate's axe run is clean in both themes.
